mainTopic: יוכבד's renewed youth and wedding, and the בנות צלפחד: the order of their names, whom they could marry, and why the tribe rule lasted only one generation
overview: The amud opens by finishing a side discussion about עמרם remarrying יוכבד. The גמרא asks how a 130-year-old woman can be called 'בַּת', and why the פסוק says 'וַיִּקַּח' (took) instead of 'took back.' רב יהודה בר זבידא answers that her youth returned and that עמרם made her a full wedding. The גמרא then returns to בנות צלפחד. Their names appear in one order by age and in another by wisdom, which supports רבי אמי's rule: honor wisdom when learning and age at a meal. רב אשי limits this rule to someone who clearly stands out. The school of רבי ישמעאל instead says all five sisters were equal. שמואל rules they could marry into any tribe, and he reads 'only within their father's tribe' as good advice. רבה challenges this from a ברייתא and answers that the tribe rule applied to everyone except בנות צלפחד. Finally, רבא learns from 'זה הדבר' that the tribe rule was only for that generation, and רב אשי explains why שחוטי חוץ is different.

steps.title: How can a 130-year-old woman be called 'daughter'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges calling יוכבד 'בַּת' when she was 130 years old.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it possible that she was 130 years old, and the פסוק still calls her 'בַּת' (a young girl)?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the wording of the פסוק 'בַּת לוי'. The woman עמרם took was יוכבד, and she was 130 years old, so how can the תורה call her 'בַּת'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בַּת' usually describes a young girl. Calling a 130-year-old woman 'בַּת' looks strange, so the גמרא wants to know what the word is hinting at. The next step proves that she really was 130.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible? (here it expresses surprise)

phrases.english: Is it possible? She was one hundred thirty years old,
and the verse calls her 'daughter'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר בַּת מֵאָה וּשְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה, וְקֹרֵא לָהּ: ״בַּת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the פסוק 'וַיֵּלֶךְ אִישׁ מִבֵּית לֵוִי וַיִּקַּח אֶת בַּת לֵוִי'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 130-year-old woman cannot normally be described as a young girl.

steps.title: Proof that יוכבד was conceived on the way to מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא shows from a פסוק that יוכבד was born just as יעקב's family entered מצרים, which is how we know her age.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חמא בר חנינא said: This is יוכבד, who was conceived on the journey and born inside the walls of מצרים. The פסוק says 'who was born to לוי in מצרים', so her birth was in מצרים but her conception was not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question by proving when יוכבד was born. She was born right at the moment the family arrived in מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses that she was born 'in מצרים', which implies she was conceived before they got there. Since בני ישראל were in מצרים for 210 years and משה was 80 at יציאת מצרים, she was 130 when משה was born.

keyTerms.meaning: between the walls (once they entered מצרים)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Ḥama bar Ḥanina said:
This is Yocheved,
whose conception was on the journey,
and she was born between the walls,
as it is written: 'Who was born to Levi in Egypt'
her birth was in Egypt,
but her conception was not in Egypt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the basis for the claim in Step 1 that she was 130.
steps.raayaObject: That יוכבד was 130 years old at משה's birth
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 26:59, 'אשר ילדה אתה ללוי במצרים', as explained by רבי חמא בר חנינא

steps.title: Her youth miraculously returned
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר זבידא explains that יוכבד is called 'בַּת' because the signs of youth came back to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why is she called 'בַּת'? רב יהודה בר זבידא said: This teaches that the signs of youth were born again in her. Her skin became smooth, the wrinkles flattened out, and her beauty returned to its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the question now that her age is proven, and then answers it. The word 'בַּת' hints at a miracle: she became young again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd word 'בַּת' is not a mistake. It teaches that יוכבד was physically restored to youth when she remarried עמרם. The question becomes the source of the חידוש.

phrases.english: And why do they call her 'daughter'?
Rav Yehuda bar Zevida said:
This teaches that signs of youth were born in her,
the flesh became smooth,
the wrinkles were straightened out,
and the beauty returned to its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי קָרוּ לַהּ ״בַּת״? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר זְבִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the question from Step 1 after the proof in Step 2, then answers it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: דרשה: the unusual word teaches a miracle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בַּת' seems to be the wrong word for a 130-year-old.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בַּת' is deliberate. It teaches that her youth was miraculously restored.
steps.whatToRemember: The word 'בַּת' for 130-year-old יוכבד teaches that she became young again.

steps.title: Why 'took' and not 'took back'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק says עמרם 'took' יוכבד, when he was really remarrying her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'and he took'?! It should have said 'and he took back'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks a second word in the same פסוק. עמרם had already been married to יוכבד, since אהרן and מרים were already born, so why does it sound like a first marriage?
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמרם had separated from יוכבד and then returned to her. The natural wording would be 'וַיַּחְזוֹר', 'he returned', so the word 'וַיִּקַּח' needs an explanation.

phrases.english: 'And he took'?!
It should have said 'and he took back'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second wording question on the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For a remarriage, 'took back' would be more accurate than 'took'.

steps.title: עמרם made her a full wedding
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר זבידא explains that עמרם celebrated a complete wedding, as if marrying her for the first time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר זבידא said: This teaches that he made her a real wedding. He sat her in a bridal carriage, אהרן and מרים sang before her, and the angels said 'אֵם הַבָּנִים שְׂמֵחָה', 'a joyful mother of children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about 'וַיִּקַּח'. The word is used because עמרם treated the remarriage like a brand-new wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וַיִּקַּח' is the word for a first marriage. The פסוק uses it to show that the remarriage was celebrated in full, with a bridal carriage, singing, and even the angels joining in.

keyTerms.meaning: an act of marriage (a full wedding)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda bar Zevida said:
This teaches that he performed for her an act of marriage:
he seated her in a bridal carriage,
and Aharon and Miriam were singing before her,
and the ministering angels were saying:
'A joyful mother of children.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בַּר זְבִידָא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָשָׂה לָהּ מַעֲשֵׂה לִקּוּחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: דרשה: the wording teaches how the event happened
steps.terutzMaskana: 'וַיִּקַּח' teaches that עמרם made a full first-time wedding.
steps.whatToRemember: Both odd words in the פסוק ('בַּת' and 'וַיִּקַּח') come from רב יהודה בר זבידא: יוכבד became young again, and עמרם made her a full wedding.

steps.title: בנות צלפחד listed by age in one place and by wisdom in another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to בנות צלפחד and notes that their names appear in two different orders in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Later on, the פסוק lists them in order of their age. Here, it lists them in order of their wisdom.
steps.whatsHappening: The side discussion is over, and the גמרא goes back to בנות צלפחד. It explains why the order of their names changes. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In במדבר 36 (when they marry), the order follows age. In במדבר 27 (when they ask משה a legal question), the order follows wisdom. The setting decides which order is used.

phrases.english: Later on, the verse lists them according to their age,
and here, according to their wisdom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the יוכבד side discussion and returns to the main topic of בנות צלפחד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The different orders of the names reflect age in one place and wisdom in the other.

steps.title: This supports רבי אמי: wisdom when learning, age at a meal
steps.stepSummary: The two orders support רבי אמי's rule about who gets honor in which setting.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי אמי, who said: At a sitting of learning, follow wisdom. At a meal, follow age.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the two orders of the names as support for רבי אמי's rule about seating people by honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When they came before משה to ask about the law, they are listed by wisdom, which matches 'בישיבה, follow wisdom.' At their weddings, a social occasion, they are listed by age, which matches 'במסיבה, follow age.'

keyTerms.meaning: a sitting for learning or judgment

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Ami,
as Rabbi Ami said:
In a sitting, follow wisdom.
phrases.notes: He means a setting of Torah learning or judging. The wisest person gets the place of honor.

phrases.english: At a meal, follow age.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from the observation in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's rule: wisdom in a ישיבה, age at a מסיבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two different orders of the names of בנות צלפחד
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule of כבוד: who gets the seat of honor depends on the setting.

steps.title: רב אשי: only when someone clearly stands out
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי limits רבי אמי's rule to people who are outstanding in wisdom or outstanding in age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That is only when the person is outstanding in wisdom, and only when the person is outstanding in age.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a limit to רבי אמי's rule. It applies only when the difference is big and clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wisdom wins in learning only if someone is clearly wiser than the others. Age wins at a meal only if someone is clearly older. Small differences do not change the order of honor.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And this is only when one is outstanding in wisdom,
and this is only when one is outstanding in age.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וְהוּא דְּמַפְלַיג בְּחׇכְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the rule of רבי אמי from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wisdom or age decides honor only when the person clearly stands out in it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי: wisdom decides at learning, age decides at a meal. רב אשי: only when the difference is outstanding.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל: The daughters were all equal
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל says the five בנות צלפחד were all equal in stature. The proof is the single word 'וַתִּהְיֶינָה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The daughters of צלפחד were equal, as the פסוק says 'וַתִּהְיֶינָה' ('and they were'). This means there was one level for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different view about the בנות צלפחד. They were all equal, so the order of their names does not show who was greater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6-8 read the two different orders of the names as a sign of who was greater in wisdom or in age. This teaching disagrees. The single word 'וַתִּהְיֶינָה' groups all five together, which shows they were on one shared level.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל
Equal, of the same weight or stature

steps.confusionAlert: This view does not use the age-and-wisdom reading of steps 6-8. If all five were equal, it makes no difference whose name comes first, so the order can change from one פסוק to the other.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
The daughters of Zelophehad were equal,
as it is stated: "And they were" —
there was one 'being' for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from the reading in steps 7-8, which used the name order to show who was greater.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five בנות צלפחד were all equal in stature.

steps.title: שמואל: The daughters could marry into any tribe
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the בנות צלפחד were allowed to marry men from any tribe. The proof is the words 'let them marry whomever they think best'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The daughters of צלפחד were allowed to marry into all the tribes. The פסוק says: 'Let them be married to whoever is good in their eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. שמואל rules that the בנות צלפחד were not limited to their own tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the first half of the פסוק, 'to whoever is good in their eyes,' as real permission. That means any tribe was allowed. This sets up a problem with the second half of the same פסוק, which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The daughters of Zelophehad were permitted to marry
into all the tribes,
as it is stated: "To whoever is good in their eyes they shall be wives";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the same daughters: whom they were allowed to marry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בנות צלפחד were permitted to marry into any tribe.

steps.title: But the verse says they must marry within their tribe
steps.stepSummary: שמואל asks himself a question. What about the words 'only into the family of their father's tribe,' which seem to limit them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But how do I explain the words 'Only into the family of their father's tribe shall they be married'?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל raises a problem against his own ruling. The very same פסוק seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the פסוק says 'only' within their father's tribe. That sounds like a real limit, which clashes with 'whoever is good in their eyes.' שמואל has to explain what these limiting words mean.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain (literally, 'fulfill') this other פסוק?

phrases.english: But how do I fulfill
"Only into the family of their father's tribe shall they be wives"?
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, במדבר 36:6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that they could marry into any tribe.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'only' seems to limit them to their own tribe, which clashes with full permission.

steps.title: It was only good advice
steps.stepSummary: The limiting words were not a command. The פסוק was giving them good advice to marry only men who were a fitting match.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק gave them good advice: they should marry only someone who is fitting for them.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers his own question. The 'only within the tribe' words are advice, not a law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the words as advice lets both halves of the פסוק stand. Legally, they were allowed to marry into any tribe. The פסוק simply recommended a suitable husband.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the בנות צלפחד could marry anyone. 'Within the tribe' was just good advice.

phrases.english: The verse gave them good advice,
that they should marry only one who is fitting for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the limiting words are advice, not a command.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'only within their father's tribe' were a binding limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those words were a recommendation to marry a fitting man. Legally, all tribes were allowed.

steps.title: רבה begins a challenge from a ברייתא about fathers and sons
steps.stepSummary: רבה objects to שמואל by quoting a ברייתא. Some מצוות were given only to the 'fathers' (the generation at הר סיני), and some only to the 'sons' (the later generations).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה raised an objection. 'Say to them' means those standing at הר סיני. 'Throughout your generations' means the generations to come. If it was said to the fathers, why say it to the sons? If it was said to the sons, why say it to the fathers? Because there are things for the fathers that are not for the sons, and things for the sons that are not for the fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts an objection against שמואל. This first part of the ברייתא is setup: it explains that the fathers and the sons each had their own מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the תורה had to speak to both generations, because their מצוות were not exactly the same. The example that matters here comes in the next step. That example will show that marrying within the tribe was a real מצוה for the fathers.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection (from an earlier source)
Fathers (the generation at סיני) and sons (the later generations)

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: ״אֱמוֹר אֲלֵיהֶם״ – לְאוֹתָן הָעוֹמְדִים עַל הַר סִינַי,
phrases.english: "Say to them" — to those standing at Mount Sinai,
"Throughout your generations" — these are the coming generations.

phrases.aramaic: אִם נֶאֱמַר אָבוֹת – לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר בָּנִים?
phrases.english: If it was said to the fathers, why was it said to the sons?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם נֶאֱמַר בָּנִים – לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר אָבוֹת?
phrases.english: And if it was said to the sons, why was it said to the fathers?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּאָבוֹת מַה שֶּׁאֵין בַּבָּנִים,
phrases.english: Because there is something for the fathers that is not for the sons,
and there is something for the sons that is not for the fathers —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an attack on שמואל's answer from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that marrying within the tribe was only advice.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the ברייתא shows that some מצוות belonged only to the fathers' generation. The next step names one of them.

steps.title: Marrying within the tribe was a real מצוה for the fathers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's example of a מצוה only for the fathers is 'every daughter who inherits must marry within her tribe.' That makes it a real command, not just advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the fathers it says: 'And every daughter who inherits a portion' must marry within her father's tribe. And the sons were commanded many מצוות that the fathers were not. So because the fathers have something the sons do not, and the sons have something the fathers do not, the תורה needed to mention the fathers and needed to mention the sons.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the ברייתא that רבה is quoting. It calls marrying within the tribe a real מצוה for the fathers' generation, which clashes with שמואל's 'good advice.' In the next step רבה points to this line to make his challenge, and step 16 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists 'every daughter who inherits' as the special מצוה of the fathers. That means the rule was binding on that generation, which included the בנות צלפחד. So how can שמואל say they were free to marry into any tribe?

keyTerms.meaning: A daughter who inherits a portion of land

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mention the בנות צלפחד by name. The challenge works because they belonged to the 'fathers' generation, and that generation was commanded to marry within the tribe.

phrases.english: About the fathers it says:
"And every daughter who inherits a portion";
phrases.notes: במדבר 36:8. The פסוק goes on to say she must marry someone from her father's tribe.

phrases.english: and many מצוות the sons were commanded
that the fathers were not commanded.

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּאָבוֹת שֶׁאֵין בַּבָּנִים,
phrases.english: So, because there is something for the fathers that is not for the sons,
and there is something for the sons that is not for the fathers —

phrases.aramaic: הוּצְרַךְ לוֹמַר אָבוֹת, הוּצְרַךְ לוֹמַר בָּנִים.
phrases.english: it was necessary to mention the fathers, and necessary to mention the sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from step 13 and makes clear the point that attacks שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that 'only within their father's tribe' was only good advice.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats marrying within the tribe as a binding מצוה for the fathers' generation. The בנות צלפחד belonged to that generation, so for them it was a command, not advice.

steps.title: רבה points to the words of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבה drives home his challenge: the ברייתא says the fathers' generation was commanded that every inheriting daughter marry within her tribe.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: about the fathers the תורה says, 'And every daughter who inherits a portion' must marry within her tribe!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה points to the line in the ברייתא that hurts שמואל. It calls the tribe rule a real command for the desert generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the tribe limit was only good advice. The ברייתא lists it as a מצוה given to the 'fathers,' and the בנות צלפחד were part of that generation. So it looks like they were also commanded.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. Used to point at the key line of a source.
The 'fathers,' meaning the generation in the desert

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
Regarding the fathers it says:
"And every daughter who inherits a portion!"
phrases.notes: במדבר 36:8. The rest of the פסוק says she must marry someone from her father's tribe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבה's challenge by pointing to the exact words of the ברייתא quoted in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that the בנות צלפחד could marry anyone and that the limit was only advice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the tribe rule a command for the whole desert generation, and the בנות צלפחד were in that generation.

steps.title: רבה answers himself: the בנות צלפחד were an exception
steps.stepSummary: רבה, who raised the question, also answers it. The command applied to everyone in that generation except the בנות צלפחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה himself raised the challenge and he himself answered it: the rule applied to everyone except the daughters of צלפחד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that רבה answered his own challenge. The tribe rule was a real command for that generation, but the בנות צלפחד were left out of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא and שמואל do not argue. The ברייתא gives the general rule for the desert generation. שמואל is talking about the special case of the בנות צלפחד, who were told 'marry whomever you think best.'

phrases.english: He raised the objection
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבה, the one who asked the question in step 13.

phrases.english: and he resolved it:
except for the daughters of Zelophehad.

steps.whatToRemember: The tribe rule was a real command for the desert generation, but the בנות צלפחד themselves were an exception and could marry anyone.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not taking back his challenge. He accepts that the rule was a command, and only carves out the בנות צלפחד as an exception.
steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: the general command did not include this specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The command covered every inheriting daughter of that generation, including the בנות צלפחד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The command covered every inheriting daughter of that generation except the בנות צלפחד.

steps.title: How do we know the rule was only for the fathers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא and asks: where do we see that the tribe rule applied only to the fathers and not to later generations?
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: about the fathers the תורה says 'And every daughter who inherits a portion.' The fathers, yes; the sons, no. From where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the ברייתא itself. It wants to know the source for limiting the tribe rule to the desert generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most מצוות last forever. So if this one stopped after the first generation, there needs to be a hint in the פסוק. The גמרא asks where that hint is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' Introduces a line from a source quoted earlier, to look at it more closely.

phrases.english: The Master said:
Regarding the fathers it says:
"And every daughter who inherits a portion"
For the fathers, yes; for the sons, no.
From where is this implied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the argument with שמואל and goes back to the ברייתא to ask for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows the tribe rule was only for the desert generation

steps.title: רבא: 'This is the matter' means only this generation
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from the words 'זה הדבר' that this law applied only to that generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the פסוק says 'This is the matter,' meaning this matter will apply only in this generation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source. The word 'this' in 'this is the matter' points to that one generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'זה' (this) as a limit: this matter, for this generation. That is why the ברייתא says the rule was for the fathers and not for the sons.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is the matter.' The opening words of the command.

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse says:
"This is the matter"
this matter will not apply
except in this generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'זה הדבר' limit the tribe rule to that one generation.

steps.title: רבה זוטי: the same words appear about שחוטי חוץ
steps.stepSummary: רבה זוטי asks רב אשי: the words 'זה הדבר' also appear about slaughtering offerings outside the משכן. Would that law also apply only to one generation?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה זוטי said to רב אשי: If so, 'This is the matter' written about slaughtering outside, would that also apply only in this generation?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה זוטי challenges רבא's reading. The same words are used for a law that clearly applies forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'זה הדבר' always means 'only this generation,' then the ban on שחוטי חוץ should also be limited, and that cannot be. So the words alone cannot be the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so.' Shows that an idea leads to a bad result.
Offerings slaughtered outside the משכן or בית המקדש, which is forbidden

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה זוּטֵי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabba Zuti said to Rav Ashi:
If so,
"This is the matter" of slaughtering outside,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:2. This is the section that forbids bringing offerings outside the משכן.

phrases.english: so too, will it not apply
except in this generation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's source from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that 'זה הדבר' limits a law to one generation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words appear about שחוטי חוץ, a ban that applies in every generation, so the words cannot mean 'only this generation.'

steps.title: There the תורה says 'throughout their generations'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שחוטי חוץ is different because the תורה says there 'לדרתם,' which shows that law lasts for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written: 'Throughout their generations.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי, who was asked the question, answers it. In the case of שחוטי חוץ, a separate word tells us the law is forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זה הדבר' alone means 'only this generation.' But by שחוטי חוץ, the word 'לדרתם' overrides that limit. The tribe rule has no such word, so רבא's reading stands.

phrases.english: It is different there,
as it is written: "Throughout their generations."

steps.whatToRemember: 'זה הדבר' limits the tribe rule to the desert generation. שחוטי חוץ lasts forever only because the תורה adds 'לדרתם' there.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה זוטי's challenge in step 19 and keeps רבא's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the other law has an extra word that changes the meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זה הדבר' would limit שחוטי חוץ to one generation too.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לדרתם' makes שחוטי חוץ last forever. The tribe rule has no such word, so it stays limited to that generation.
